memo.verdict: Park. Neutral with a bullish bias on valuation; conviction low (a working hypothesis); re-tested on 2026-10-23 (the Q3 2026 report) and 2027-02-03 (the FY2026 report). The framework's park rule is tripped twice, by management ('No mediocre management', RA 3, E 1, BB 4) at D and business quality ('Business', E 2, BB 2) at D; predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) and trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) are both C and do not trip it. The record does not argue against the gate: the price is a reason to watch closely, not a reason to override a gate whose purpose is exactly this profile. Progress to Early-Stage if the Q3 2026 report carries no new items affecting comparability and positive operating cash flow, followed by a Q4 2026 adjusted EBITA margin above 7.5% and leverage below 3.0x, at any price below about SEK 24; or, before those dates, a permanent chief executive with a Nordic services record is appointed with the same conditions pending. Invalidate on an equity raise; a Norwegian segment margin below 2.0% in any quarter; leverage above 3.5x after Q3 2026; or a third consecutive third quarter with write-downs. The case is compelling on arithmetic and not compelling on evidence: a case to watch with dated triggers, not yet a case to own.
case: Thesis. Green Landscaping is a recovery case in a leveraged roll-up, priced as a distressed equity. At SEK 16.2 (2026-10-12) the shares trade at 3.9x earnings two years out, the lowest point in the stock's own history, because the equity is a quarter of an enterprise value that itself trades at an ordinary 8x EBITA; almost any recovery that does not need new equity clears the 20% bar from here. The folder does not yet show that the recovery has started, and the people running it are interim.

The change is internal and a reset rather than a build. The chief executive of eleven years left on 16 Jul 2026, the day before the Q2 2026 report; a board member with a restructuring record became acting chief executive the next day and within two months launched Green Performance (profitability, working capital, governance), took SEK 79m of charges, filed a police report against a German subsidiary's former owner and appointed four country managers (22 Sep 2026). The chairman changed in May 2026 to the chief executive of the largest shareholder. Dividend zero, buybacks halted, acquisitions paused (only Finke in H1 2026) so debt can fall. The two principal owners bought through the fall to 38.94% combined; the departing chief executive sold 38.45% of his holding. Internal forces (RA 2, E 1, BB 1) at C: at least four of twelve forces strong (chief executive change B; other leaders B; strategy change B; standards improvement B), two more real (perimeter reduction B: three loss-making Swedish units liquidated removing a SEK 50m to SEK 60m annual EBITA drag, Svensk Jordelit sold for SEK 37m; acquisitions D: engine paused, post-deal margin decay of 4.6 percentage points, a fraud-related write-down), passing the screen's rule of three; but a caretaker chief executive and dangerous leverage (3.4x against 2.5x) are both present, and guidance raised (F: all three medium-term targets of 10% sales growth, 8% EBITA margin and 2.5x leverage missed four quarters running and not rebased), balance sheet (F: over-utilised, the programme is about reducing utilisation) and shareholder returns (F: dividend zero, buybacks halted) run the wrong way. Price rises D: indexation only (about 65% of contract value indexed; more than 90% of maintenance revenue), nominal and lagged a year; Norway cut price to hold volume. Ullenvik's record: Swedol stores 47 to 107, sales SEK 1,378m to SEK 3,500m, operating margin 5.4% to 10.0% by FY2018; Alligo adjusted EBITA margin 6.4% in FY2025 with -2.2% organic in his last full year.

The external forces net to a mild headwind only beginning to ease (RA 1, E 1, BB 1 at C). About 60% of sales are municipal and public under three-to-five-year contracts growing about 4% a year, non-cyclical (demand C); the private 40% and the landscaping half are contracting. Competition D: construction generalists with empty order books bid into Nordic landscaping tenders; Norway's segment margin 13.4% (FY2022), 9.9% (FY2024), 3.7% (FY2025), 4.1% (Q2 2026), a 740 basis point contraction in 2025; fewer bidders noted by management on 17 Jul 2026 is one quarter's observation; Inderes places pricing normalisation in 2027. Supply side D: personnel about 30% of costs, subcontractors 25% of operating costs, fuel 79% of energy use, annual indexation lag; Swedish agreed minimum wages rise 8% for 2027 (a group point about installers, a question for the Q3 call). Own cycle B: organic growth +11% (Q1 2026) and +6% (Q2 2026) after five negative quarters (Q1 2025 -18%, the mildest winter in fifteen years), backlog up 6%, Q2 sales beat of 6%; partly weather. Macro C: net interest SEK 157m in FY2025 on year-end net debt SEK 2,510m, about 6.3%, so 100 basis points is about SEK 25m pre-tax, about SEK 0.33 of EPS, about 13% of our FY2027 estimate; the hiking path re-marked up works against Green; municipal budgets hold a stable 5% to 6% allocation for green areas. Disruption C, political and regulatory C, weather the catch-all. No demand force meets the 'Demand Inflection' test.
counter_case: At its strongest: Green was never a compounder but a multiple arbitrage with a shrinking core. Organic adjusted EBITA fell about 7% a year from 2019 to 2024 while acquisitions added 38% a year of sales to 2023; cash conversion was 28% over five years, not in one bad year but in six; acquired businesses lost an average 4.6 percentage points of margin within two years of purchase as their founders left; the controls (a SEK 30m underwriting cap, local finance functions, no internal audit) failed in three countries at once; and the man who built the group sold 38% of his shares the moment he could. On this reading the Nordic margin is not in a trough but at its structural level for a labour-heavy, price-taking service business once acquisitions stop flattering it. FY2028 adjusted EPS is about SEK 3.0 rather than SEK 4.0, leverage stays above 3.0x, the Q3 2026 peak forces a conversation with the banks, and the equity is refinanced at the shareholders' expense. The research's own analysis of competing hypotheses gives this "false friend" profile zero hard inconsistencies and puts the bear case at medium-high probability. The founder who knew every subsidiary and had just lost his job sold 38.45% of his shares near the low; the uncharitable reading is that the person with the most information chose to sell, and the record cannot settle it from the folder; it is the one fact that argues the owners who are buying know less than the one who is selling.

The bounded-downside argument does not rescue it. Other Europe's EBITA is about SEK 300m (a 17.5% rolling-twelve-month margin on about SEK 1,700m of sales; 59% of group EBITA in 2025), a pre-tax, pre-interest divisional profit, so the like-for-like multiple is an enterprise multiple: at 4x, the price the group pays for private targets, about SEK 1,200m, a third of the SEK 3,590m enterprise value; at 8x about SEK 2,400m, two thirds; only at 12x does it cover the enterprise value. It covers the SEK 914m market capitalisation at any of those multiples, but that is not a bound, because the market capitalisation sits beneath SEK 2,668m of debt that ranks ahead of it. On the enterprise lens a fall from 8x to 6x EV/EBITA leaves the equity at nothing; the framework's caution that multiples fall further than people accept applies to the enterprise multiple here.
triggers: - 23 Oct 2026, Q3 2026 report: no new items affecting comparability (invalidate if more than about SEK 20m in any quarter after Q3 2026; alarm on any item in Q4 2026); positive operating cash flow; leverage at or below 3.7x (invalidate above 3.5x after Q3 2026); Norway segment margin (alarm below 4.1%; invalidate below 2.0%; confirm above 5.0%); Sweden margin (invalidate below 4.5%); Other Europe margin (invalidate below 14%); working capital to sales (invalidate above 8.2%); organic growth (alarm below 4%); any comment on the 8% Swedish minimum-wage rise for 2027 and the indexation lag.

- 3 Feb 2027, FY2026 report: Q4 adjusted EBITA margin above 7.5% and leverage below 3.0x, the earnings review's own tests, adopted; these two would turn 'Disruption abating' to C or B, 'Major CfC Clearing' to C, and are the progression trigger at any price below about SEK 24; a Q4 margin above 7.5% or leverage below 3.0x would also trigger sell-side raises.
- Cash conversion above 50% for four consecutive quarters: the condition under which the 'Foundations' counter-hypothesis (specific failures, not the model) becomes the record's view.

- A permanent chief executive: probable at about 70% within twelve months of 16 Jul 2026; confirming if an external operator with a Nordic services record; its appointment with the dated conditions pending is the alternative progression trigger; alarm if none by 16 Jul 2027.
- An equity raise: the invalidating event; a SEK 500m rights issue at about SEK 12 cuts the eighteen-month return to about 27% a year at the blend and about 10% at 6x, a loss on the adverse path.
- A third consecutive third quarter with write-downs invalidates.
